meta.note: Flagged for Review. Every item here is something we could not confirm from an official source, or an irregularity we found in an official feed. Per the brief, none of these blocks the merge. Each carries the source link so you can check it yourself.

flags.title: No official NFL depth chart exists
flags.detail: The brief asks the system to know when 2nd, 3rd or 4th string players replace starters. The league does not publish depth charts. A direct fetch of https://www.nfl.com/teams/kansas-city-chiefs/depth-chart returned the NFL's 404 page ('404 - Flag on the Play'). Depth order must therefore be derived, and any derived order is an estimate, not an official fact.
flags.impact: Blocks REQ-010, REQ-011, REQ-012 as literally specified.
flags.action: Decide on the snap-share inference approach (suggestion S-007).

flags.title: The NFL publishes no official betting lines or odds
flags.detail: No price appears anywhere on nfl.com. The league's own exclusive data distributor for sports-betting data is Genius Sports, so the only league-authorised route to official betting data is a commercial agreement with them. Without it, every market comparison on this project depends on a non-official price source.
flags.impact: Blocks market comparison, CLV measurement and therefore every validation gate.
flags.action: Decide whether to license a feed, or run the leaderboard on an explicitly non-official price source with that caveat published.

flags.title: Official injury report: body-part column is empty for 97.6% of rows
flags.detail: Of the 254 players listed on the official Week 10 report, only 6 carry any text in the Injuries column (Patrick - Concussion, Yankoff - Knee, Harrison - Groin, Ben Brown - Knee, Carlton Davis III - Knee, Henderson - Illness). The remaining 248 rows are blank. Counted directly from the ingested official data.
flags.impact: Any signal that keys off injury type (for example, hamstring versus ankle) cannot be built from this feed as published.
flags.action: Look for the body-part detail in another official surface, or drop injury-type signals from scope.

flags.title: Seahawks show 'No Injuries Reported' while NFL.com news reports their starting QB ruled out
flags.detail: The official Week 10 injury report shows 'No Injuries Reported' for Seattle. The official NFL.com news rail on the same page carries the headline 'Sam Darnold ruled out for Seahawks' Week 10 game vs. Raiders; Drew Lock expected to start again'. A player moved to injured reserve leaves the injury report entirely, so the report understates unavailability for teams with IR placements.
flags.impact: Injury tracking built on the injury report alone will miss exactly the most severe cases. Directly undermines REQ-009.
flags.action: Add the official transactions feed (IR / PUP / NFI / elevations) as a mandatory companion to the injury report.

flags.title: Snapshot taken on Thursday; most game statuses not yet filed
flags.detail: Retrieved 2026-11-12 (Thursday). Only 6 of 254 listed players carry a game status: 5 Out and 1 Questionable, 0 Doubtful. The remaining 248 Game Status cells were empty on the official page at retrieval time. This is the expected mid-week state, not a data error, but it means the snapshot must not be read as final.
flags.impact: Any conclusion drawn from game-status counts this week is provisional.
flags.action: Re-ingest after the final report is filed and diff against this snapshot.

flags.title: Requirement rows have no official external source
flags.detail: The 'every table row links to an official site' rule is a rule about DATA. Requirement rows are governance rows derived from the owner's project brief, which has no public URL. They are labelled 'Internal brief' and are exempted from the source assertion.
flags.impact: None - but the exemption is deliberate and should be reviewed rather than assumed.
flags.action: Confirm the exemption, or supply a canonical URL for the brief.

flags.title: Injury-report definitions and deadlines could not be confirmed on any official domain
flags.detail: The categories themselves (DNP / Limited / Full and Out / Doubtful / Questionable) were observed directly on the official report. Their written definitions and the filing deadlines were NOT: operations.nfl.com/gameday/nfl-game-status returned 404, operations.nfl.com/inside-football-ops/health-and-safety/injury-report returned 404, and nfl.com/injuries/inactives returned 404. The commonly repeated definitions and deadlines are therefore published on this site as 'not verified', never as fact.
flags.impact: We cannot attach an official probability to a designation, which several modelling approaches would want.
flags.action: Locate the policy text on an official domain, or estimate the mapping empirically from our own history once we have it.

flags.title: Week 10 bye teams are inferred, not read
flags.detail: DEN, PHI, CHI and TB do not appear on the official Week 10 injury report. The official standings show all four with exactly 9 games played, while every team appearing on the report with 8 games played is playing this week. The conclusion that those four are on bye is consistent across two official sources but was not read from the official schedule.
flags.impact: Low, but it is an inference and is labelled as such.

flags.title: Home and away designation is not asserted
flags.detail: The official injury report lists two clubs per matchup without an explicit home or away label in the retrieved markup. Rather than guess, this site presents each matchup as an unordered pair. Home/away is a material model input, so this is a real gap, not a cosmetic one.
flags.impact: Any home-field or travel-adjusted model input is unavailable until resolved.
flags.action: Read the official schedule and populate home/away as a verified field.

flags.title: Every correlation value is blank
flags.detail: The brief asks us to determine correlation values. No league-official, government-official or regulator-official source publishes a player-prop correlation matrix, and no historical joint-outcome data has been ingested. The correlation register therefore states the structural direction of each relationship and leaves the magnitude cell empty and flagged.
flags.impact: Parlays and prop combos cannot be priced honestly yet. This is the honest state, not a gap to be papered over with invented numbers.
flags.action: Obtain historical joint outcomes, then estimate and hold out (suggestion S-006).

flags.title: Branch naming deviates from the session-<id>/<task> convention
flags.detail: The brief asks each session to work on a branch or worktree named session-<id>/<task>. This session's branch name is fixed by the platform as arena/87deb7ab-nfl1 and the session is not permitted to rename it or create another branch. All work is on that single branch with a non-overlapping file scope.
flags.impact: Coordination still holds; the naming convention does not.
flags.action: Accept the deviation, or have the platform assign conforming names.

flags.title: The repository was empty - there was no site to review
flags.detail: git log shows a single commit (5aeb599, 'Initial commit'). The only tracked file was README.md, 6 bytes, containing '# NFL1'. There was no code, no data, no site and no prior analysis. The brief asks for a line-by-line review of the repo against official sources; there was nothing to review, so this became a greenfield build instead.
flags.impact: If you expected an existing site to be reviewed, the content you were expecting is not in this repository.
flags.action: Confirm whether a different repository or branch holds the existing work.
